house-spot.purpose: Spot colour when no album cover applies (light theme).

hairline.purpose: 1px lines between credit entries, rows and editor groups (10% ink).

spot.purpose: Per-album colour from cover art: coverColour() picks the strongest saturated hue bin, fitSpot() fits it to >=4.6:1 text contrast on the current background, refitSpot() reruns on theme change (app.js:297-358). Registered via @property, crossfades 700ms. --accent/--accent-soft(13%)/--selected(10%) derive via color-mix in oklab.

on-color.purpose: Text, ticks and icons on the spot or status colours (art badge, phone brand icon, checked and indeterminate ticks, activity icons, destructive fill). White in light; booklet black in dark because the dark spot and status colours are fitted light. --on-accent aliases it (app.css:68, 97, 126, 139).

display.purpose: Album title in the booklet-spread header; 30px on phones.

headline.purpose: Folder and library titles; 30px on phones.

section-head.purpose: Editor group heads, set in the spot colour.

body.purpose: Everything else; 15px on phones; inputs 16px on phones.

label.purpose: Credit-sheet field labels, sub-lines, table head (600).

track-number.purpose: The only tabular figures in the system: zero-padded track numbers.

mono.purpose: Raw tag names, tag keys, update steps.

themes.mechanism: Light on :root; dark under @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) :root:not([data-theme=light]) and :root[data-theme=dark] (app.css:33-128).

narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "Liner Notes"**

Codetta reads like the credits pages of a beautifully made CD or LP booklet: every track gets the credits page it deserves. The ground is booklet stock (near-white, faintly cool) or booklet black, the type is ink in one display-grade grotesque, and structure comes from rules rather than boxes: a 1.5px ink rule opens each list, hairlines separate entries, and editable fields sit on a hairline like a printed credit line until touched. It is an operating tool, dense and calm, with the music's own artwork as the only full colour on screen.

The one moving part of the identity is the spot colour. Each album lends the interface a single colour lifted from its cover art, fitted for text contrast against the current theme, and crossfaded when you move between albums. It marks the active track, changed fields, the editor's section heads, the album's genre chip, links, focus and selection. The library, search results and coverless folders fall back to the house spot (teal). Everything else is ink, stock and grey.

It refuses the category default of a grey dashboard with one fixed blue accent and a boxed data table. It is not dark-and-nerdy, cute or corporate; confidence comes from exact, quiet typesetting, not decoration.
keyCharacteristics: One typeface (Schibsted Grotesk), heavy and tight for titles, regular for credits.
Rules, not boxes: 1.5px ink rule over every list, 1px hairlines between entries.
One spot colour per album from its cover; house teal when there is none.
Album art is the only full colour; covers are square (2–3px corners).
A folder that is one album becomes a booklet spread: 200px cover beside a 52px title, with repeating columns dropped.
Light and dark themes are equals; the spot is refitted on every theme change.

rules.name: The One Borrowed Colour Rule
rules.body: The only chromatic UI colour on screen is the open album's spot (or house teal). Never add a second brand accent, a fixed blue, or decorative colour; album art supplies the rest.

rules.name: The Fitted Spot Rule
rules.body: Any colour taken from artwork must pass through `fitSpot()` before it touches text: 4.6:1 against the current background, refitted when the theme changes. Never paint raw cover colour onto UI.

rules.name: The Ink Button Rule
rules.body: The primary action (Save, Sign in) is solid ink on stock, not the spot. The spot marks state and identity; ink marks commitment.

rules.name: The Tabular Track Number Rule
rules.body: Tabular figures are used only for track numbers ("01"–"99", zero-padded, weight 600, app.css:482). Times, counts, versions and sizes keep the font's default figures (`font-variant-numeric: normal`).

rules.name: The Heavy-and-Tight Rule
rules.body: Any title 19px and up is weight 800 with negative tracking (−0.02em to −0.045em). Body and credits never go below 400 or get tracked.

rules.name: The Flat Page Rule
rules.body: Nothing in the reading flow (rows, folders, headers, fields) carries a shadow. If it's on the page, it's ruled; if it floats, it may lift.

rules.name: The Ink Rule
rules.body: Every list starts under a 1.5px ink rule and separates its entries with 1px hairlines. Never box a list in a bordered card.

dos: Do derive every chromatic UI colour from `--spot` (`--accent`, `--accent-soft`, `--selected` via `color-mix`), and let the house teal stand in when there is no cover.
Do open every list with a 1.5px ink rule and separate entries with 1px hairlines.
Do set titles in Schibsted Grotesk 800 with negative tracking, and reserve tabular figures for track numbers.
Do drop columns that would repeat the same value on every row of a single album.
Do keep primary actions solid ink, 6px corners, and say what will happen ("Save to 5 tracks").
Do use the motion tokens (120 / 200 / 260ms, ease-out in, ease-in out); phone sheets slide 340ms; the spot crossfades 700ms; all of it stops under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
Do keep 16px inputs and 44px touch targets on phones, and honour safe-area insets.
Do bundle every font and icon; no CDNs, no inline scripts or handler attributes (CSP).
donts: Don't add a second accent, a fixed brand blue, gradients or decorative colour; album art is the only full colour.
Don't use raw cover colour for text or UI without `fitSpot()`.
Don't box lists or rows in bordered cards, or put shadows on anything in the reading flow.
Don't round covers or the logo's square beyond 2–3px.
Don't extend the floating layer's softer corners (10–16px) to page-level surfaces.
Don't add uppercase tracked section labels, kicker lines above titles, or text-glyph icons; use inline SVG. (Format codes such as FLAC in the small badge are data, not labels.)
